pr_title: Allow POST/PUT without Content-Length or chunked
pr_body:
**Allow POST/PUT without Content-Length or chunked**

If I understand HTTP 1.0 rfc1945#section-8.3 PUT and POST should return 400. In contrast to HTTP 1.1 and the referenced rfc7230#section-3.3.3 which may return 411. As this class (referenced above) seems to be used for request, response sections of above RFC-s fall out of consideration.

The following changes made:

- Updating MessageBody's For method to reject when no Content-Length *only* for HTTP 1.0
- Removing LengthRequired reject reason, which is internal and not used elsewhere
- Updating unit tests

Fixes #29398
pr_comments: I am considering adding a fix for the other bug mentioned in #29398 what do you think? It is just about casing on the http method name.

Let's keep them separate, this one changes protocol behavior and we want it to be as clear as possible for future reference. It looks about ready to merge regardless.

issue_context.title: Allow POST/PUT without Content-Length or chunked.
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/28565

Kestrel refuses POST and PUT requests with a 411 if they don't have a `Content-Length` or `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` header.
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/702b937577122445498a2d800c7ca1782a1b3556/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http/Http1MessageBody.cs#L182-L188

That doesn't match the RFCs and limits client compatibility.

https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#section-3.3.3
>    6.  If this is a request message and none of the above are true, then
       the message body length is zero (no message body is present).
...
>    A server MAY reject a request that contains a message body but not a
   Content-Length by responding with 411 (Length Required).

https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-4.3.3 (POST) doesn't say anything about 411s or requiring a non-zero body or the associated headers.

Kestrel should default to no body when there is no content-length or chunked for HTTP/1.x.

This is a non-issue for HTTP/2 since the introduction of the END_OF_STREAM flag.

Note, there's another bug with this logic anyways: #26803

From the original discussion: @Dzoge

> 
> Hey
> I ran into an issue with some clients calling my REST sevice that do not send Content-Length header when the body is empty and Transfer-Encoding is not chunked. When this happens Kestrel returns HTTP 411 Length Required response.
> 
> I was looking for a way to intercept the request and manually inject Content-Length header with 0 but could not find the way to do it.
> 
> The server is running without a reverse-proxy in front of it and the requests go directly to Kestrel docker pod.
> 
> I searched the Kestrel source code and found a check for that specifically:
> aspnetcore/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http/Http1MessageBody.cs
> 
> Line 182 in 857bb0f
> 
>  // If we got here, request contains no Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding header. 
> 
> but I could not find any way to override this behavour.
> Is there any way to configure or intercept this behaviour and manually add a Content-Length header with 0 value or somehow make it pass this validation?
> 
> There is another way to solve this issue by putting a reverse-proxy in front of Kestrel that will fix the headers, but I don't want to introduce a new component in the chain if it is other way.

@dzoge, can you clarify which clients you were testing with?

If we want Kestrel to be used as a reverse proxy (YARP) we should support this case.

To manually test this during the change I used the Sample app in the Kestrel project, and cURL for Windows.

```ini
curl.exe -X POST http://localhost:5000 --http1.1
curl.exe -X POST http://localhost:5000 --http1.0
```
